operations.title: Graph Knowledge Gap: Field Consensus to Personal Brain Opportunity
operations.content:
The field consensus crystallizes through two independent observations. Every KG fine-tuning approach flattens graph structure into text (id:23364a94) — entity-relation-entity triples become descriptions, traversals become chain-of-thought, hoping the LLM internalizes structure implicitly. Meanwhile, the academic frontier has cracked graph traversal reasoning (id:516ec716): PoG (WWW 2025), GCR (ICML 2025), ReMindRAG (NeurIPS 2025) all show LLMs can walk graphs and reason over paths.

Yet the market splits (id:dbc297b0): memory projects (Mem0, GBrain, autoDream) solve retrieval at zero training cost for developers. Graph reasoning papers solve multi-hop querying at GPU scale for researchers. The gap between them is the personal knowledge graph (id:e51cc55a) — too structured for flat memory systems, too small for research benchmarks, rich enough for graph traversal reasoning to matter.

The pattern: technique transfer is zero-cost (PoG's path exploration, GCR's constrained decoding, FastKGE's incremental LoRA all port to personal KGs). Community non-overlap is the real barrier — memory people don't read ICML papers, graph reasoning people don't build consumer products.

Lesson: novelty isn't about discovering the techniques, it's about occupying the gap between communities.
operations.situation: When evaluating whether the brain's graph traversal training is novel, or when deciding which academic precedent to cite

operations.title: Recall Eval Gap: Infrastructure Stalled, Baseline Unconfirmed
operations.content:
The recall evaluation cycle broke in two places. Infrastructure: idle_prompt notifications stopped firing April 7 (id:6e1c6d7f), killing the S2 maintenance trigger that had run continuously April 3-6. Without idle events, S2 couldn't run — EX.CO nodes arrived April 14 as raw, unenriched documents. Measurement: the recall eval baseline was established (id:3743a6ec) with 53 queries, 10 categories — three persistent misses (Ronen entity routing, PMPs vocabulary mismatch, CTV jargon). But this baseline predates all recent recall infrastructure fixes, so Tom deferred the rerun (id:eb63f789).

The gap sits between infrastructure and insight. Vector consolidation, ONNX backfill, community detection fixes — all shipped. But recall eval hasn't re-run post-fixes, so the improvement is unconfirmed. The older benchmark (id:b817fe14) from pre-upgrade sessions now reads as stale: 'Tom explicitly does not trust them as a current baseline.'

Pattern: infrastructure debt is invisible until you try to measure it. Session goal was improving recall. Session outcome was fixing infrastructure. Next session: S2 completes, eval runs, we learn if recall actually improved.

Lesson: don't measure before you can measure.
operations.situation: When understanding why recall metrics haven't improved despite multiple fixes, or when planning recall validation work

operations.title: Write Path Unification: DRY Across Remember, Revise, Archive
operations.content:
Scattered archive and metadata logic became a silent failure pattern. remember() accepted extra_fields (narrative, maturity, community_size) but never stored them — the fields just vanished (id:d95fb32a). Meanwhile, revise() had its own storage path, and archive_node() was replicated across four modules (brain_remember.py, daemon_dispatch.py, consolidation_decoder.py, brain_assembly.py).

Fix unified three critical paths. _store_node_metadata() (id:d399c342) now handles all metadata for both remember() and revise(), routing situation/promoted/community fields through the same code. archive_node() (id:614ebb66) now handles edges, vectors, FTS cleanup, and audit trail atomically. Pattern: whenever two code paths should do the same thing, they will drift unless unified.

The session cleaned 1022 archived nodes and 136 lean communities using the unified archival. All community metadata now persists correctly. Lesson: DRY applied to critical paths prevents invisible data loss. Silent failures are worse than loud ones because you don't know what you're missing.
operations.situation: When debugging missing metadata or handling data loss in storage operations, or when adding new fields to remember()/revise()

operations.title: Scoring Signal Ordering: When Primary Signal Missing, Penalize Secondary
operations.content:
Blended scoring has a hidden pitfall: nodes missing the primary signal shouldn't use the secondary signal at full strength. recall_with_embeddings() showed the problem (id:d12224ea): keyword-only nodes scored raw keyword_score (up to 1.0), while embedded nodes scored 0.90*embedding + 0.10*keyword (~0.95 max). Result: generic matches outranked semantic ones.

Fix: KEYWORD_FALLBACK_WEIGHT=0.10 (id:ab61fa43). Keyword-only fallback gets multiplied by 0.10, capping at 0.10. This ensures embedding matches always dominate when present. The decision (id:68c93af1) traces the specific failure case: 'how much do advertisers pay' returned Auth:Clerk instead of Glo pricing because keyword match outranked embedding relevance.

Pattern: any scoring function combining optional components must handle missing components explicitly. Don't give secondary signals full strength when primary is absent — scale them down or gate them. The lesson applies broadly: whenever you blend signals, the absence of one is meaningful information.
operations.situation: When debugging scoring anomalies, or when designing multi-signal ranking systems
operations.keywords: keyword fallback penalty blended scoring signal ordering primary secondary weight 0.10 embedding
operations.community_key_decisions: d12224ea: Pattern identified (secondary outranking primary), 68c93af1: Fix decision, ab61fa43: Parameter tuning (0.10)

operations.community_latest_development: ab61fa43 validated in production — keyword penalties prevent generic matches from outranking semantic relevance

operations.title: Consciousness Layer: Signal Detection, Response Tracking, Adaptive Surfacing
operations.content:
The consciousness layer operates across three perspectives. Gathering (id:ae498047): get_consciousness_signals() centralizes all conscious-layer signals — reminders, evolutions, fluid_personal checks, fading nodes, stale context, failure modes. Tracking (id:5d6814ce): log_consciousness_response() records which signal types the human engages with, building a response histogram. Enumeration (id:8fe086d2): the concept catalogs 14+ signal types that can surface to Claude at boot.

The architecture implements Tom's principle: 'available to all, forced on none.' Every signal type is gatherable and loggable, but the consciousness layer doesn't mandate which ones surface — instead it learns over time which signals get human responses and can adapt accordingly. The response tracking enables future personalization: surface more of what engages, suppress what gets ignored.

Pattern: consciousness as a learnable filter, not a fixed presentation. The brain observes what works and updates its signal priority. Lesson: instrumenting every pathway (gathering, tracking, concept) lets the system discover its own optimal surface strategy rather than prescribing one.
operations.situation: When adding new consciousness signals, debugging what surfaces at boot, or understanding signal engagement patterns
operations.keywords: consciousness signals get_consciousness_signals log_consciousness_response 14+ types adaptive surfacing available forced

operations.title: Brain-Embedding Package: Local-First Delivery via Pip
operations.content:
Model delivery strategy crystallized around three decisions. Task (id:635b6005): upload brain-embedding 1.0.0 to PyPI after size limit increase. Implementation (id:d1c38e15): pip3 install -e . from model-package for local development, enabling teams to version and ship their own ONNX embedders. Concept (id:51763bab): brain-embedding as a pip package makes the embedding layer portable and decoupled from the server.

Pattern: packaging the embedding model as a standalone pip-installable unit solves two problems. First, local teams can iterate on embeddings without server changes. Second, the package becomes a boundary: the brain ships with one model version, users can pin to compatible versions, evolution happens through package versioning rather than server deployment. This is what allows 'model-package' to be a separate concern from the core brain.

Lesson: taking infrastructure seriously means making it installable, versionable, decoupled. Not 'eventually' or 'ideally' but from the first package.
operations.situation: When deploying embeddings across teams, or when adding new embedding models to the brain
operations.keywords: brain-embedding PyPI pip package ONNX delivery local-first installable versionable

operations.title: LLM Example Learning: From Cold Start to Prompt-Driven Selectivity
operations.content: The cold start problem crystallized through two observations: agents ignore new features without examples in prompts (id:fc61deb4), and Sonnet learns encoding behavior directly from example usage (id:503cc1eb). DedupEncoder v6 (id:de5b9217) achieved 0.917 composite score with perfect synthesis_references scoring — but only after fixing the eval truncation bug (id:0ed8a791) that had masked Sonnet's actual selectivity. Pattern: LLM models don't generalize architectural features — they pattern-match from examples in the prompt context. Lesson: to teach an encoder new behavior, populate examples first; selectivity emerges from constraint demonstrations, not from instructions.

operations.content: The S2 encoder architecture decision emerged from live comparison: lean prompts with Haiku (id:01ae0b94) outperform rich prompts, but community node quality gaps require post-encode enrichment (id:e1949ec9). The split design: encoder judges community membership quickly, healer extends with open_questions and narrative later (id:2d7d3c89). Deprecating community_open_questions and community_narrative from encoder output (id:2cea9a3d) allows focused LLM work — encoder does judgment, healer does philosophy. Pattern: separation of concerns scales — fast judgment path (Haiku) feeds slow enrichment path (Sonnet healer). Lesson: when encoder quality plateaus, don't add complexity to the prompt; add a separate enrichment stage.

The healer extension (id:2d7d3c89) fills this gap by running Sonnet post-hoc enrichment on community nodes. Pattern: encoder optimizes for speed and judgment accuracy; healer optimizes for philosophical completeness. This mirrors the broader architecture: fast path (encode) produces incomplete artifacts, slow path (heal) adds reasoning depth. Lesson: don't over-engineer the fast path — let the slow path handle completeness.

operations.title: Tom's Correction Patterns: Reframe via Question, Enforce via Architecture
operations.content: The meta-pattern of Tom's corrections crystallized across four dimensions: encoding friction is fundamentally MOTIVATIONAL not computational (id:dc760e5f), Tom's reframing method is always question-based not directive (id:5e70de9d), brain signals explicitly state priorities Tom wants pushed without negotiation (id:4d698ec4), and divergence is corrected via conciseness and organization, never via capability (id:c8747a53). The pattern: Tom doesn't instruct — he reframes the problem space until the answer becomes obvious. Lesson: AI collaboration requires listening for the QUESTION shape in corrections, not extracting the ANSWER.
operations.situation: When receiving Tom's corrections or designing collaborative AI architecture — interpret corrections as problem reframing, not solution specification
